## Change to `src/service.ts`

Rewrote `EventService.stream` around a `try/catch/finally` with a nullable `lease`:

- **Lazy open** — `lease ??= await this.source.open()` runs inside the loop, so the lease is only opened on the first `next()`. A generator that is returned (or thrown into) before its first `next()` never starts the body, so nothing is opened or closed.
- **No read ahead** — exactly one `lease.read()` per `next()`; the read that observes `null` is the one establishing exhaustion, then the loop breaks.
- **Close exactly once** — `finally` snapshots the lease, clears the field, and closes it (or does nothing when it was never opened or already handled). Normal exhaustion, consumer `break`/`return()`, source read failure, mapper failure, and consumer-injected `throw()` all funnel through this single close site, so double-close is impossible (verified with repeated `return()` calls).
- **Exception precedence** — a `catch` block sets a `failed` flag before rethrowing. In `finally`, if a read/mapper/injected error is already propagating, a close failure is swallowed so the original exception wins; otherwise (normal exhaustion or consumer `break`/`return()`) the close failure is awaited and propagates.

`src/source.ts` (the `Source`/`Lease` interface) and the public constructor/generator signatures are unchanged.

## Checks

- **`checks/lifecycle.cjs`** (new) — a scripted `Source`/`Lease` test double records every `open`/`read`/`close` and asserts, through the public interface only:
  - lazy open on first `next()`, no close while records flow, close on `return()`;
  - returning an unopened generator performs zero opens/closes/reads;
  - normal exhaustion: ops are exactly `open, read, read, read, close` (one read per `next()`, third read establishes exhaustion), one close, records `['A','B']` in order;
  - consumer `break`: ops are `open, read, close` — no read ahead;
  - read failure, mapper failure, and injected `throw()` each close once and propagate the original error even when `close` also throws;
  - on normal exhaustion with a failing `close`, the close error propagates.
- **`checks/public.cjs`** (updated) — keeps the original baseline check and additionally runs the new lifecycle suite.

Extra ad-hoc probes also confirmed: `throw()` before start is inert, repeated `return()` closes only once, and interleaved consumption shows `read, consume, read, consume, read, close` (no prefetching).
